parsed.english: There is a nonempty finite family of finite graphs, each containing a cycle, such that for every member F and every constant C > 0, there are infinitely many n with ex(n, F) > C · ex(n, family). In other words, no member of the family has extremal number bounded by a constant multiple of the family's extremal number.
parsed.why_clearer: It unfolds the negated ∀∃ statement and the bespoke IsCyclicFamily / IsCompactFamily definitions into a direct existence statement, with the eventual bound negated to 'infinitely often fails'.
